label: H.R. 10707
title: Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act of 2026

items.snippet: This bill authorizes grants and makes other changes to facilitate the practice of medicine by internationally trained physicians who are lawfully present in the United States and graduated from a medical school outside of the United States or Canada.

items.item: Department of Health and Human Services
items.snippet: Specifically, the Department of Health and Human Services may award grants for states and territories to establish or expand programs that allow such physicians to…
Specifically, the Department of Health and Human Services may award grants for states and territories to establish or expand programs that allow such physicians to practice medicine under the…

Specifically, the Department of Health and Human Services may award grants for states and territories to establish or expand programs that allow such physicians to practice medicine under the supervision of a…

The bill also exempts under certain circumstances such physicians from the cap on full-time equivalent residents that is otherwise applicable for purposes of graduate medical education payments under Medicare.

lobbying.caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.
lobbying.amount_note: Amounts are the income or expenses reported on the whole LD-2 filing, not money spent on this bill.

caption: This shows who the bill names and who lobbied on it. It does not show who gains or loses, and lobbying can be for or against a bill.

S000510.label: Overlap, not proof of influence.
S000510.caption: Money from this member's itemized individual donors (over $200) whose self-reported employer falls in an industry that also has a client lobbying on this bill. Correlation only; not a quid pro quo. Donors give to campaigns for many reasons, and a lobbying client may have opposed the bill.
S000510.note: None of the lobbying clients on this bill matched an industry rule, so there is nothing to compare.
